entry.title: Harbour Festival posters, 2026
entry.content: The brief was simple: make people stop on the pier. Each poster shows the harbour at a different hour, from high water to low, in two flat colors.
entry.summary: Six posters for this year's festival, each one a different hour of the tide.

entry.title: A new identity for the Net Loft café

link.title: A new identity for the Net Loft café

entry.content: The café kept its name and lost its clip-art fish. The new sign is painted by hand, the menu is set in one typeface, and the cups are plain white with a small blue stamp.
entry.summary: A name, a sign and a menu for a café in an old fishing loft.

entry.title: Keeping a commonplace book of type

link.title: Keeping a commonplace book of type

entry.content:
A commonplace book is a notebook of things worth keeping. Mine is full of letters: painted signs, cast-iron numbers, tickets.1 Here is how I keep it.

The rules

  1. Write the date before anything else.
  2. Copy the source with every note, even a page number.
  3. Never delete an entry; cross it out instead.

Sketch - draw the letter, then write where you saw it.

Index - the last four pages, by street.

A worked example

Letter Where Notes
R the ferry office painted, 1950s
7 mooring post 7 cast iron
& the bakery gold leaf

Good lettering is everywhere once you start looking.

When the notes moved to a computer I wrote a tiny script to rebuild the index:

2025-11-03  R  ferry office   painted
2025-11-04  7  mooring post   cast iron
2025-11-06  &  bakery window  gold leaf

  1. I started it on a rainy holiday and never stopped. ↩
entry.summary: My notebook of letters seen around town, with the index that keeps it useful.

entry.title: Designing a tide table people can read

link.title: Designing a tide table people can read

entry.content: The harbour office printed its tide table in seven-point type. I redrew it with bigger numbers, one color for high water and one for low, and a note on the back in plain words.
entry.summary: The old table needed a magnifying glass. The new one fits on a postcard.

entry.title: Signs of the harbour: a lettering walk

link.title: Signs of the harbour: a lettering walk

entry.content: Start at the ferry office and end at the bakery. Ten signs, three of them older than anyone who works there.
entry.summary: A one-hour walk past the best painted signs in town.

entry.title: Color notes from a gray winter

link.title: Color notes from a gray winter

entry.content: Thirty-one paint chips, from almost white to almost black. The palette is now the basis of the festival posters.
entry.summary: Every day for a month I matched the sky to a paint chip.

entry.title: Why I sketch on paper first
